assumptions: Adjusting coupling parameters to 0.90 captures sufficient variance.
Stochastic drift can be isolated and measured via mean absolute differences.
definition.falsification: If divergence variance delta remains below 0.03 under the adjusted coupling parameter, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling coefficients and perturbation baselines are adjusted to capture subtler trajectory variations.
definition.uncertainty: Environmental noise or insufficient trajectory separation may still affect measured deltas.

definition.method: Run simulation with adjusted coupling coefficient to measure trajectory variance delta.
definition.source:
def experiment(inputs):
    import random
    params = inputs.get('parameters', {})
    seeds = inputs.get('seeds', [111, 222, 333])
    random.seed(seeds[0])
    coupling = params.get('coupling', 0.90)
    baseline = [random.random() for _ in range(20)]
    trajectory_a = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.05) for x in baseline]
    trajectory_b = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.05) + 0.02 for x in baseline]
    diffs = [abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(trajectory_a, trajectory_b)]
    mean_diff = sum(diffs) / len(diffs)
    return {'measurements': {'divergence_variance_delta': [mean_diff]}}
definition.stop: Stop after confirming variance delta across seeds.
